recipes.name: Grilled Shrimp and Apple Skewers
ingredients_raw: 2 Gala apples, cored and cut into eighths

steps.text: Whisk together the honey, olive oil, basil, strawberry jam, red pepper flakes, garlic, red wine vinegar, lemon juice and white sugar in a small bowl. Place the apples and shrimp into a large resealable plastic bag. Pour the marinade over the shrimp and apples, seal the bag, and shake to coat; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat.
Thread the shrimp and apples alternately on 4 metal or soaked wooden skewers. Discard the remaining marinade.
Cook the skewers on the preheated grill until the shrimp are opaque, about 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Shrimp and Apple Skewers
raw_recipe.description: Shrimp and apples are marinated in a sweet and spicy sauce, then skewered and grilled. Serve over white rice, noodles, or a mixed green salad.

review.reviewBody: These shrimp were so tasty! I don't like hot fruit, so I did not use the apples on the skewers, but didn't want to lose out on the apple flavor, so I added 1.5 T. of applesauce to the marinade (apple juice works, too), and used brown sugar instead of white. Let the shrimp marinate 2 hours, threaded them onto skewers, boiled the marinade 3 minutes to use for basting, and they were out of this world! I served them with garlic butter rice and sauteed zucchini.... delicious, delicious dinner!
I doubled the red pepper, basil, and garlic. Then I added a 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika. I didn’t want to use skewers so I put it all in a grilling pan. Very delicious.

These shrimp were so tasty! I don't like hot fruit, so I did not use the apples on the skewers, but didn't want to lose out on the apple flavor, so I added 1.5 T. of applesauce to the marinade (apple juice works, too), and used brown sugar instead of white. Let the shrimp marinate 2 hours, threaded them onto skewers, boiled the marinade 3 minutes to use for basting, and they were out of this world! I served them with garlic butter rice and sauteed zucchini.... delicious, delicious dinner!

FABULOUS! I used chipotle powder instead of red pepper flake which really complimented the strawberry. Marinated it for 2 hours and doubled the sauce as suggested by previous members which was a fabulous idea. We decided to serve the skewers elegantly over spinach greens and thinly sliced red onion which was delicious. The extra marinate was then used as the dressing. Perfect!
Double sauce! I skipped the grill and used an iron skillet. One batch of sauce sautéed apples. The other was for the shrimp. This was side dish at a dinner party and everyone asked for the recipe!

With apologies for changes: Doubled marinade. Did not use grill, but added chopped granny smith apples, diced onion, celery, and bell pepper to marinade. Sauteed marinated shrimp on stove top. Removed shrimp and sauteed marinade til vegs. softened. and marinade thickened. Served over green salad, using marinade as dressing. Despite my changes, I rated this recipe 5 stars because it was delicious.

The shrimp had a WONDERFUL flavor but the apples all broke off the skewers as they cooked on the grill. Next time I'm going to grate apple into the marinade for the flavor but omit it from the skewers, leaving only shrimp. Then serve with a great salad and egg potato salad.

This was a very tasty summertime grilling recipe! For the marinade I used apple juice, instead of the sliced apples, and brown sugar instead of the white. This marinade would be great on other types of seafood as well!

Best shrimp skewers I've had in a long time. I omitted the sugar and they were fantastic - not sure what the sugar would have brought to the dish since the jam already makes it sweet. I halved (width-wise) the 1/8 apple wedges since I was breaking skewers to get the apples on in their original humongous state. I followed advice of others and put the skewers through the skin - so i didn't have any problem with them falling off on the grill. And the apples were delish - I wouldn't omit them.

Based on some other reviewer's suggestions, I added 2 TB of applesauce to marinade and used brown sugar instead of white. I used fresh basil and doubled the amount. I marinated the shrimp for about 2 hours, then sauteed them in a hot skillet over the stove. Loved the taste, thanks Moonroze!

I think this is one of the best things I have ever cooked on allrecipes. I did this for a get together I had in my back yard. I also did another recipe for shrimp skewers that had zucchini and onions on them. Those were good, but couldn't compare to these and since we didn't have enough, everybody was fighting over these! Things I changed: I let them marinate for a lot longer, like 2-3 hours. And I doubled the marinade recipe, I had huge shrimp, and I usually always end up doubling it any recipe that has a marinade. Good thing I did or it wouldn't have been enough. One last thing, we added pineapple because we happened to have a bunch in the fridge and I knew it would be good, and it was. I think the amount was around 2 cups, but I can't be sure...about as much as the apple amount. You need to add pineapples to this for sure!

A very different way to enjoy shrimp, and it's so good! I added some red onion to the skewers and they added a great flavor. I thought the marinade was going to make the shrimp very sweet but no and the apple adds a little bit of acidity that breaks the sweetness on this recipe. The family loved it!

The marinade added just the right amount of sweetness to the shrimp with overpowering them. I didn't have strawberry jam but used grape jam and it came out delicious. I wouldn't bother with the apples the next time.
I cooked this shrimp recipe on the BBQ and they turned out Fantastic. Easy & Flavorful! The whole family loved them and wants more! Highly recommended.
Easy to make and the apple and shrimp complemented each other well. Also, baked apple is always a treat.

I read the reviews because that always helps a ton. I used a 2 pound bag of raw shrimp and I figure my family can take the tails off themselves. I doubled the sauce recipe too because my kids always like sauce. I had only really nice basil olive oil which probably made it even better. I used brown sugar because it's usually better and raspberry jam. I buy chopped up garlic in a jar so you don't have to chop it and I always guess on the amount. I used a granny smith apple and honey crisp. It marinated for about 1.5 hours. I will continue when I cook it.

Made as directed, although since it was raining I baked at 400 for 8 minutes as suggested by another reader. Did not place on skewers, just put in baking pan. Was delicious, and apples were just the right amount of softness, without being mushy. I was a bit worried about red pepper, but added great flavor without being to much spiciness for me. Definately want to try on grill next time, and would probaly add pineapple as suggested as well! But family loved this - a keeper for sure!

This was ok. Some changes I made because it was all I had. I had to use red raspberry preserves instead of strawberry. I used green apple instead of Gala. I used metal skewers instead of wood. Cooked on the stove instead of grill. I liked the way it taste, but I didn't think it was the best.

This recipe is wonderful! I made no changes to the marinade, but I did add fresh pineapple to the mix as suggested by someone else. I'll definitely make this again and with a little more crushed red peppers to give it an extra kick.
yup yup yup.....this is a keeper....
